text:
leo: Quick sync: we need a concise playbook for pin aliasing and the canonical stable-ref semantics. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a suggested minimal schema.

priya: high level: keep canonical identity = content_hash. aliases are just human-friendly labels and can map to hash+metadata. important for audits.

rafael: +1. two main tensions: ppl want semver for humans, infra wants content-hash for immutability. we should support both but make clear rules for resolution.

jin: suggestion: resolution order: 1) exact content_hash match, 2) explicit pin_id match, 3) semver range resolution (most recent that satisfies), 4) alias fallback. deterministic and logged.

meera: on deprecation: add `deprecation_window_days` and `sunset_policy` enum (`auto_replace | notify_only | block_new_pins`). that lets us automate safe rollouts.

leo: proposed minimal schema (compact):

```
{ "pin_id": "pin-2026-06-42", "canonical_hash": "sha256:abc123...", "aliases": ["stable-chat-1", "semver:1.x"], "compat_tags": ["kv-cache-compatible", "quant-friendly"], "deprecation_window_days": 14, "sunset_policy": "auto_replace", "release_notes_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/pins/pin-2026-06-42" }
```

priya: keep `aliases` lightweight. avoid embedding full rollout rules. the runtime should keep affinity and routing metadata internal. only expose `aliases` and `compat_tags` if tenant opts in.

rafael: compatibility tags are powerful for routing decisions. but need a whitelist and schema so customers can't invent arbitrary tags that break infra. we'll keep central registry of allowed tags.

jin: migration note: clients should first try hash resolution and fallback to alias/semver. SDKs must surface a clear `resolved_pin` with both `pin_id` and `canonical_hash` so apps can log and assert.

meera: for semver ranges, use explicit rules: ranges resolve to the highest non-deprecated pin that matches. if highest is deprecated within `deprecation_window_days`, prefer the next one and emit a `deprecation_warning` in response.

leo: auditability: every resolution must emit `resolution_path` in telemetry (list of steps tried). short example in response body: `{ "resolved_pin": "pin-2026-06-42", "resolution_path": ["semver:1.x","alias:stable-chat-1","hash:sha256:..."] }`

priya: security/tenant isolation: aliases are tenant-scoped by default, unless explicitly global. default prevents name collisions across tenants.

rafael: edge case: alias migration when a pin is replaced by a different hash. We should support `alias_history` to trace prior mappings for debugging. small list is fine.

jin: RFC checklist i'll draft: 1) canonical_hash primary identity, 2) alias/semver support + resolution algorithm, 3) compat_tag registry, 4) deprecation/sunset policies, 5) telemetry fields (`resolved_pin`, `resolution_path`, `deprecation_warning`), 6) tenant scoping defaults, 7) SDK guidance and sample payloads.

meera: ops: ensure storage index supports queries by alias and semver efficiently. also GC policy for `alias_history`.

ops-bot: note: create ticket INF-4210 to track RFC + infra work.

leo: action items: jin -> RFC draft + pseudocode resolver; rafael -> compat tag registry proposal; priya -> tenant scoping + console UX; meera -> storage & GC notes. will sync next Tue. Thanks all :rocket:
